differences.what: the east range's frontispiece over its side door (T-3110): the print's stone frontispiece between pilaster strips from grade (x 345-398 px) carries a small round-arched light filled with an ornamental grille (x 362-382, y 1045-1070, about 2.4-3.1 m), a paired light in the upper storey (x 355-385, y 940-985, about 4.7-5.9 m) and, through the eave, a coped gable between pinnacles with a finial (apex x 372, y 835, about 8.65 m); the build's range wall ran plain under its hip with two rows of reconstructed sash. Built (bays.p_door): 3.0 m wide, 0.1 m proud, the grilled round-headed light and the mullioned pair on its axis, a coped gable of pitch 1.5 between pinnacles; its lights render within about 5 px of the print's rows

the frontispiece's place along the range: its axis renders at x 394 against the print's 373, about 1.15 m west, because r3b's 18th Street wall (u -8.5 to -4.6, the 1911 sheet's rectangle) holds it; the print's frontispiece straddles the sheet's junction of r3b and r2, which nothing on the print marks. A K08 bay stands on one wing's wall, so moving it onto the print's axis means re-cutting the wings or carrying a bay across a junction

the side door under the frontispiece's round-arched light: a narrow door at the walk (x 368-382, y 1092-1170, its head about 1.8 m) with a glazed panel; the build has none there (no K01 wing or K08 bay cuts a door)
differences.how: T-1890 cuts it (bays.p_door's lowest storey): K06's new k06.opening.door_glazed_narrow, one leaf with a solid panel to 0.85 m and a light of glass over it, 0.75 by 2.0 m in the kit's moulded surround, on the frontispiece's axis; K08's new `door` key runs it down through the plinth to the step and breaks the plinth either side. Re-rendered, the door stands about 13 px wide from y 1083 to the build's grade at about 1160, against the print's 14 px from 1092 to its walk at 1171: the whole wall's foot renders about 12 px over the print's walk through this camera, and the door's axis about 20 px east of the print's with the frontispiece (its place, above). The ornamental iron over its glass is finer than a visitor reads at the walk and is within tolerance

differences.what: the east range's openings: the print's 18th Street face is blank ashlar between pilaster strips and string courses, with one column of lights a storey at x 283-300 (u about -12.6), the frontispiece's lights and nothing else between the turret and the gabled section; the build had three columns of sash on r2 and one on r3b. r2 now carries the one column at s 5.3 and r3b's light is taken out (the frontispiece stands there)
differences.how: T-1890: that column of lights now stands in the frontispiece round it (bays.p_east_gable), the lower light at 1.55 m and the upper at 4.7-6.15 m, the print's upper light within about 10 px

differences.what: a hooded slate dormer on the east range's roof between the turret and the frontispiece (x 300-345, y 870-950, its stone face under it to about y 990): the build's wing hip carries no dormer (a K01 wing's roof takes none)
differences.how: T-1890, read again at full size: the slate between the turret and the frontispiece is not a dormer on the range's hip but the slate roof of a second stone frontispiece, whose coped gable between pinnacles rises through the eave at x 272-318 (its apex behind the utility pole) and whose white-capped ridge runs back into the range's roof at about y 876-888; the 'stone face under it' is that bay's front, carrying the range's one column of lights. bays.p_east_gable stands it on r2's 18th Street wall in p_door's dressing; it renders between x 263 and 313 against the print's 272-318 (L-kimball-1801-east-gable-1890)

differences.what: a tall stack rising behind the frontispiece's gable (x 337-403 px, its cap at about y 780, about 10 m): the build has no stack over the east range (a K01 stack stands only in the main block's roof)
differences.how: T-1890 tried it (2026-10-27): a stone stack in the east range's roof on the print's line of sight, its cap at about y 776. One picture cannot fix its depth, and on the build's range hip (its ridge 8.3 m) the stack stood about 4 m of bare shaft over the slate, where the print shows only its cap clearing the slate behind the frontispiece, which stands to about y 795 (about 10 m at the wall's depth) against the build's hip at about y 865 there. So the stack was taken out: it waits on the range's roof, which in this print stands far higher than the build's (the frontispiece's place, above, moves with it)

differences.what: the east range's eaves: about 5.9 m at the turret end through this camera against the build's 6.35 m, which T-3076 read off the Taylor print at 6.2-6.4 m; the two pictures disagree by about 0.4 m
the east range's roof: the print's slate face rises steeply from the eave to about y 800 (about 9.6-10 m) over the frontispiece; the build's 45-degree hip rises to the same line from this eye

the north-east turret: the print's cone stops in a truncated neck at about 9.6 m with no finial (y 843), the build's runs to a point about 10.1 m and a finial to 11 m; the Taylor print of c. 1895 shows the finial, so the 1965 top is a later loss T-1890 sizes the turret's finial to the Taylor print's, 2.5 m over its cone, as the earlier evidence for 1904; this 1965 photograph's truncated neck is the later fabric. T-1890 (the Taylor print's turned finial over a plain collar): through this camera the build's collar rim renders at about y 835 against the print's truncated neck at about y 844; over the neck a faint pale shaft with knobs may stand against the bright sky (x about 255-260, y about 765-840), too washed out to read

the gabled section's 18th Street face: the print's round oriel, two storeys on corbels (x 430-505 px, y 780-1000) under a balustraded balcony with an open loggia behind it, three round-arched lights under it (x 436-539, y 1020-1065) and the coped gable over (apex x 497); the build's p_gable is a flat pavilion with transomed pairs. The Taylor print's match record carries the same difference (open there) — T-1890: rebuilt to the print: a round oriel on the shallow pavilion's face, its bow 2.7 m on the chord and 0.6 m out, from the 5.0 m floor to a 9.2 m wall top on six stepped corbel courses down to 3.8 m, its two transomed lights bent to the bow, under a moulded cornice and the round stone balustrade the print carries on its top; the principal storey's three round-arched lights under it, 0.5 m clear each. Through this camera the oriel's width, its corbel, its balcony and the arched lights now stand where the print's do, the balcony's rail a little (about 0.5 m) over the print's

the flank section's top: the print's third storey of paired lights under a cornice, a gabled wall dormer with a fan (sunburst) panel and a finial (x 700-800, y 400-520) and the corbel table under them (x 630-900, y 650-700); the build carries the section's wall up under K08's low hip. The Taylor print's match record carries the same difference. Built (T-1890, bays.p_flank): the second storey carried up to a corbel table whose top stands at 9.45 m (a 0.25 m course on stepped corbels down to 8.6 m; the print's at about 9.5-9.6 m), the third storey over it to a 12.4 m wall top (the print's cornice about 12.5 m) with a pair of lights in two tiers on the axis and a single light at the west end, and a coped wall dormer 1.4 m in from each corner with a carved fan in its tympanum, a pinnacle on each shoulder and a finial to 15.2 m (the print's about 15.15 m); the dormer's apex renders within about 10 px of the print's, the corbel table within about 15 px

the main block's flank stack: the print's square stack with its heavy cap stands at x 611 (its cap at y 490), about 90 px (about 3 m) east of where the build's (u 5.0) renders; the Taylor print also puts it about 2-2.5 m east of the build's. Moved (T-1890): to u 1.8, v 1.0, where this camera's and the Taylor print's lines of sight cross, in the walls' pale stone, 0.9 m square, its cap at 16.0 m (the Taylor print's; this one reads about 15.5 m); its shaft renders within about 10-30 px of the print's (x 611)

the round tower: the print's cone is broader and lower than the build's (its eave about y 520 across x 765-1005, its finial's tip at y 183), where the build's narrow cone rises far over it; and its axis renders about 37 px west of the print's (the Taylor print holds it within 16 px). The Taylor match record's open 'tower's form' item T-1890 rebuilds it to this photograph and the Taylor print: a shaft 2.2 m across (this print's about 110 px at about 54 px a metre) blank over its principal storey, five corbel courses from 7.9 to 8.9 m (this print's 8.03-8.89 m), a stage 3.7 m across (about 200-210 px here) with its two lights where this print has them (x 835-860 and 920-945; rendered within about 5 px), its cornice to 11.26 m and its cone to 16.69 m (this print's eave about 11.1 m and apex about 16.4 m); its axis renders within about 2 px of the print's

the loggia's carving, the front's bow and pavilion, the mansard's faces, hooded dormers and cresting, and the corner's arches: read here at the angle the Taylor print reads them, and no difference beyond its match record's
colour: the stone's tone and the slate's, in a monochrome print
the rear (east) wall, the court side and the south wall: this camera cannot see them
1965 fabric: the window air-conditioners, the iron fence, the pole, the hydrant and the lamp; not 1904 and not built

the tower's finial: this print's stands about 1.6 m over a crocketed collar at the cone's apex (its tip y 183, about 17.95 m), shorter than the Taylor print's c. 1895 one (about 19.6 m), which the build follows at 19.29 m as the earlier evidence for 1904; the two pictures disagree by about 1.6 m (T-1890)

the flank section's west corner (T-1890): the print rounds it from the corbel table up (x 620-700 px), with a light in the round and a low railed roof behind its cornice; the build's p_flank stands square there, the wall dormer's kneeler run out over its shoulder
differences.how: T-1890 rounds it (bays.flank_round): a round oriel 2.0 m across and 1.0 m out of the 18th Street wall, centred 0.3 m east of the section's west corner, which its ring buries under at least 0.15 m of walling; it stands on the corbel table's line (9.45 m) on four corbel courses to the section's own wall top (12.4 m), with one light (0.75 by 1.3 m, sill 9.95 m) turned 20 degrees toward the avenue in place of the square corner's single light, and over its moulded cornice a flat roof inside a stone balustrade. Re-rendered, the round's outer edge falls at about x 635 against the print's 625 and its light at about x 647-672, y 620-680 against 652-672, 632-672; the balustrade stands where the print's rail does over the cornice

differences.what: the flank stack's head (T-1890): the print's cap flares out as a bell over the shaft (x 580-650, y 480-520 px); the build lays a slab 0.3 m proud, the outline within about 0.3 m and the Taylor print reading the shaft round where this one reads it square

the frontispiece's paired lights (T-1890): the print's transom divides the two tiers about equally (at about 10.9 m); K06's transomed pair puts its bar about 0.3 m higher, the two lights and two tiers as the print has them

the wall dormer's carving (T-1890): the print's fan is finely ribbed in a moulded arch and its pinnacles crocketed; the build lays thirteen plain rays, a ring and a hub, and plain pinnacles, at the print's size
the coping and walk T-3206 lays for 1904
differences.how: the 1965 photograph shows the house after the lawn's coping was gone; the 1904 boundary is read off the Taylor print

differences.what: the 18th Street hooded dormer's hood (T-1890): the print's slated front stands wider than the face at its foot and sweeps in to a narrow top under a pale cresting along its ridge, where the build's hood rose straight from the face's own width; the hood now flares 0.2 m wider than the face each side and 0.2 m out at its foot and keeps its 0.4 m top, its foot within about 5 px of the print's and its top about 13 px narrower. The print's foot sweeps out in a concave bell where the build's runs straight, its shelf is a slim moulding where the build's is a 0.12 m stone slab, and its ridge cresting is not built
1965 fabric: the gabled section's loggia glazed in, a sash in each of its two openings under the gable; the c. 1895 Taylor print shows it open, and the 1904 build follows the print (T-1890)

the pier and downpipe where the gabled section meets the main block (T-1890): a plain stone strip from grade to under the main cornice (x 537-550 px, about u -0.1-0.45 through this camera), with a capital at the principal storey's head (y about 970) and another under the cornice (y about 820), and a round downpipe close against its east side from the gutter to grade (x 550-557); the build's wall ran plain there and carried no pipe on the 18th Street flank
differences.how: T-1890 builds the pier (bays.p_pier, 0.55 m wide on the 18th Street wall's east end, 0.1 m proud, to 8.34 m with a band at 5.0 m and a plain cap) and the copper downpipe at u 0.8 (rainwater.downpipes); re-rendered, the pier's face falls at about x 531-550 and the pipe at 552-557, within about 6 px of the print's. The capitals' carving is the kit's plain cap and band, within tolerance

differences.what: the round's support: the print carries the section's corbel table round under the round, its carved blocks following the curve (x 625-700, y 700-760); the build's table runs straight along the section's face under the round, the round's own four stepped courses behind it
differences.how: T-1890: the round's place, size, light, cornice and railed top match the print (above); the table's blocks stand at the same height and depth (about 0.85 m) either way, so whether they turn with the curve is a detail of the dress under the 1 ft bar

differences.what: the turret's and the tower's cones: the print's are slated as the mansard is, in level courses in the roof's own tone, where the build laid both in the K08 kit's plain slate colour, which rendered as smooth grey cones far paler than the roofs beside them. T-1890 slates both as the house (bays.turret and bays.tower roof.slated_as_house), their courses mapped round each cone and up its slope from its eaves; they now render in the mansard's dark coursed slate (L-kimball-1801-cone-slate-1890)

the second frontispiece's gable (T-1890): the print's apex is behind the utility pole, so its height and pitch are not read; the build's (pitch 1.2, apex about 8.5 m) stands its pinnacles about 10-15 px over the print's and its kneelers about 8 px over, about 0.3-0.4 m

the range's cornice at the frontispieces (T-1890): the print's cornice stops at both bays' pilaster strips, where the build's 0.3 m eave box ran across both bays' faces and hid the top of p_door's paired light; r2's and r3b's eaves are pulled in to 0.05 m so both bays rise clear of it

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
